events.title: Crusaders Capture Jerusalem
events.description: After a siege of about five weeks, the armies of the First Crusade broke into Jerusalem on July 15, 1099. They took the city from the Fatimid garrison, and a large part of the population was killed in the assault.
events.significance: The capture was the high point of the First Crusade. It led to the founding of the Crusader states in the Levant, and the region stayed contested for generations.

events.title: Rembrandt van Rijn Is Born
events.description: The Dutch painter and printmaker Rembrandt is traditionally said to have been born in Leiden on July 15, 1606. He was the son of a miller. Some scholars think 1607 is more likely.
events.significance: Rembrandt became one of the great masters of the Dutch Golden Age. He is known for his command of light and shadow and for the emotional depth of his portraits.

events.title: The Rosetta Stone Is Found
events.description: During Napoleon's campaign in Egypt, French officer Pierre-François Bouchard found a slab of dark stone in the town of Rosetta. It carried the same decree in three scripts.
events.significance: The stone gave scholars the key to Egyptian hieroglyphs. Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher them, which opened ancient Egyptian civilization to modern study.

events.title: Napoleon Surrenders to the British
events.description: After his defeat at Waterloo, Napoleon Bonaparte gave himself up to Captain Frederick Maitland aboard HMS Bellerophon on July 15, 1815. He had hoped to find refuge in Britain.
events.significance: His surrender ended the Napoleonic Wars. The British exiled him to the remote island of Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.
